chapter: Annex, Cadillac and the Ory-Oliver band
title: Annex band size and the district's dance halls
summary: Cabarets used only piano, violin and drums; full bands played the dozen dance halls, such as Rice's and the 101 Ranch.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: What kind of bands did they have at Anderson's Endings?

Well, I tell you, the band we had there was piano, violin, and drum. I was playing piano. Pete Buckeye was playing violin. Chris Minor was playing drum. They didn't usually have a big band with trumpets and trombones? Oh, no. That's the hammer. Now, where they had the full bands, that was in the dance halls. Well, they had about a dozen dance halls. Who were some of the dance halls? Rice's?
Rice's? Rice's? They had the Rice Dance Hall.
Oh, gee, they had George Full Coats.
George Full Coats. Oh, gee, they had George Full Coats. George Full Coats. Oh, yeah. They had the full bands, that was in the dance halls. They had about a dozen dance halls.
Who were some of the dance halls? Rice's?
They had Rice Dance Hall. They had the 101 Ranch. Ball D.
Ball D. Ball D. Yeah, do you remember that?
I don't know. That's where Richard M. Jones and Ernest Rogers and Louis Nelson and Joe Oliver. Who else? Richard Jones told me he played at Aberdee's, right? I don't know.
Well, I tell you, they had a house. I had a sporting house of Louise Aberdee and Louise Blackenstein. But Richard Jones, I know he played in the parlors.
